newsitem.title: USA: U.S. DoT - ValuJet can resume flights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DoT - ValuJet can resume flights.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transporation said Thursday that Valujet Airlines is "fit, willing and able" to resume its domestic flights.

A Department statement said the management of the low-cost carrier, grounded June 17 following a safety inspection of its operations started after its Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades May 11, killing all 110 on board, was found to be fully qualified to oversee operations.

It also said ValuJet had sufficient funds to allow it to resume scaled-back operations without economic risk to customers and that it had taken steps to strengthen management and procedures and was positively disposed to comply with all relevant laws and regulations.
Following remedial action, the FAA on Aug 29 gave ValuJet approval to resume flying, but Transportation held up approval pending comments by the public and other interested parties.
